questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Unlike most food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means that:

options.text: Within minutes of being consumed, the alcohol reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
The alcohol never gets removed from the body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Once it is in your system, your body gets rid of the alcohol quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of being consumed, the alcohol reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly without needing to be digested. It reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: Before every ride, it is important to check all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check the spokes for bends or damage, check the tire tread and condition, and check all the lights. The seat fabric does not need to be checked before each ride.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Are not as effective at protecting your eyes as eyeglasses.
Are not effective in providing any protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your entire face. Regular eyeglasses are not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Which of the following surfaces does not provide poor traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all provide poor traction. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: If you are riding in the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are likely riding in the best position to be seen.
You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
The driver will most likely assume you are there.
You are discouraging other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in the event of a crash?

options.text: No, clothing is not really for protection.
No, clothing is more of a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces injury risk in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, are made of sturdy material, and fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: Which of the following is not important when looking for a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, such as cracks or loose padding.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your entire head, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: Which types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night:

options.text: Wear reflective clothing to stay safer.
It is unsafe because drivers cannot see your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing to stay safer.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night to make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: one front, one rear, and one emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, you can help others see you by:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing, keep your headlight on, and use your turn signals to help others see you.

questions.question: Before riding your motorcycle, check everything except:

options.text: That both brakes work and turn on the brake light.
That the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil level, and all lights (headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light). You do not need to check the paint.

questions.question: Which of the following does not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and pants, ankle-covering boots, and gloves. A baseball cap does not provide the protection of a helmet.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots that are too small to matter.
Have blind spots that you must check by turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you must check by turning your head.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.
